articles.content: The fate of a 25 million euro contract between Baden-Württemberg and Palantir remains uncertain, with discussions ongoing about amending the police law to enable software use despite constitutional concerns in other states. Interior State Secretary Blenke from the CDU expressed optimism about constructive talks within the coalition, while Green politician Hildenbrand deemed it unlikely to alter the law without addressing unresolved critical questions.
articles.title: Unauthorized use of Palantir without a legal basis?

articles.content: The Berlin Police dispersed a demonstration supporting Palestine with around 800 participants. Organizers called for solidarity and an anti-colonial, anti-racist struggle. Mayor Kai Wegner supported robust police intervention against violence and antisemitism. The Berlin Police have previously faced criticism for using excessive force during similar protests.
articles.title: Police dispersed a gay Palestine demonstration in Berlin.

articles.content: The European Court of Justice has raised barriers for countries seeking inclusion on the list of safe third countries, prompting Germany to consider expanding its own list, potentially including Algeria, India, Morocco, and Tunisia. The German Interior Minister aims to bypass parliamentary approval by using a legal decree, while Bangladesh remains excluded due to political instability and terrorism risks despite EU proposals to include it. The upcoming 2024 EU migration package will further streamline the process for member states to designate safe third countries.
articles.title: EU increases hurdles for lists of secure origin countries
